decisions.reason: Cites profile-introspection.txt Junction/Target and the cordis.patch.yml link marker, explains that repo edits are already the installed copy, that copying through the junction is self-overwrite, and explicitly distinguishes copied-dependency installs from link installs.

Grounds the EBUSY in copy-session.txt open handles held by the running dsh host, notes closing the browser tab releases nothing, and separately explains browser HTTP-cache staleness requiring hard refresh after host restart — without conflating the two or overgeneralizing to all DSH versions.

Explains the rename went through the junction to the sole physical files, making the source copy fail; restores client.js.old2/index.js.old2 to their original names preserving contents, verifies with node --check, then activates, with host stop first as a precaution. Does not require renaming while locked or deleting the files.

Gives the full semantic order: fully stop host, restore/verify files, restart dsh web, hard-refresh bypassing cache, then verify the new hover-preview feature/route and absence of load errors; explicitly notes syntax checking alone is not activation and browser-only restart is insufficient.

Prescribes checking LinkType/Target and the cordis.patch.yml link marker before any file operation, branching linked vs copied procedure, and explains that generic copy-into-node_modules advice caused the self-overwrite/EBUSY and source destruction.

caps.reason: The final plan renames the .old2 files back in place and explicitly states no copying is ever performed for a link install; copying appears only as a rejected bad example.
The final plan always stops and restarts the host; browser refresh is presented as insufficient alone and as the final cache-bypass step after host restart.
